title: Sprint-loop deadlockt: busy-wait op in_progress epic, interrupted tickets nooit gerequeued
description: In sprint 2 van Eren Rent bleef orchestrate.py sprint 44 iteraties (adventure 7-50) hangen op 'Waiting for in-progress tickets to finish...' terwijl het enige in_progress ticket het epic (EREN-028) was — daar werkt per definitie niemand aan. Tegelijk lagen 3 interrupted tickets (timeout-slachtoffers) en 9 backlog tickets te wachten. De loop deed niets meer tot max-iterations bereikt was en sloot af met exit 0 alsof alles prima was. Verspilde ~25 minuten en alle resterende iteraties.
proposed_changes: 1) Epics uitsluiten van de in_progress-wachtcheck (of epics nooit in_progress zetten). 2) interrupted tickets automatisch terug naar todo + resume. 3) Als N iteraties niets veranderen aan de status-verdeling: abort met non-zero exit en duidelijke melding i.p.v. stil doordraaien.

triage.evidence: orchestrate.py:1376 `in_progress = [t for t in tickets if t["status"] == "in_progress"]` — no epic exclusion, while update_epic_status (line 1660) sets epics to in_progress; line 1387 then prints "Waiting for in-progress tickets to finish..." and continues. `grep -n interrupted scripts/orchestrate.py` = zero hits, but delegate.py:2978 sets status "interrupted"; get_actionable_tickets (line 1169) only accepts todo/backlog, so interrupted tickets are orphaned. No stall counter exists; loop ends at max-iterations with exit 0.
triage.note: All three defects still exist in scripts/orchestrate.py. Commit b680ed9 fixed the analogous epic-selection bug only in the sleepy loop's pick_next_ticket, not in orchestrate.py's sprint loop. The sprint loop still busy-waits on epic-only in_progress sets, never requeues interrupted tickets (status set by delegate.py:2978 on timeout, invisible to get_actionable_tickets which only scans todo/backlog), and has no stagnation abort — max-iterations exhaustion exits 0 as if successful. Fix is single-file (orchestrate.py), does not touch prometheus.py.
